subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: What security and ownership boundary should the browser-login handoff surface use before implementation?
rationale: The feature exposes authenticated browser state and requires product choices about core versus plugin UI ownership, operator scopes, redaction, write-action gates, and same-state resume policy that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Operator-scoped handoff panel
options.body: Build a first-party or approved browser-plugin Control UI surface that is read-only/status-first, includes target profile/tab context, gates write actions explicitly, and resumes the agent against the same browser state.

options.title: Wait for plugin UI entry points
options.body: Defer implementation until the generic plugin UI entry-point contract lands, then implement browser handoff as plugin-owned UI under that reviewed contract.

options.title: Defer to CLI/manual docs
options.body: Keep the current browser CLI and manual-login documentation as the supported path until browser preview and handoff become a higher-priority product area.

recommendation.title: Operator-scoped handoff panel
recommendation.body: Build a first-party or approved browser-plugin Control UI surface that is read-only/status-first, includes target profile/tab context, gates write actions explicitly, and resumes the agent against the same browser state.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from the canonical issue comment plus browser runtime/docs and recent plugin Control UI tab history.
